column1: The successes and failures of the Doble brothers and their steam cars
column2: 多布尔兄弟和他们的蒸汽汽车：成功与失败

column1: When primitive automobiles first began to appear in the 1800s, their engines were based on steam power.
column2: 19世纪，早期汽车刚问世时，发动机依靠蒸汽动力运转。

column1: Steam had already enjoyed a long and successful career in the railways, so it was only natural that the technology evolved into a miniaturized version which was separate from the trains.
column2: 蒸汽动力早已在铁路上成功运用了很长时间，因此，这项技术后来发展出一种可独立于火车运行的小型化形式，也就十分自然。

column1: But these early cars inherited steam’s weaknesses along with its strengths.
column2: 不过，这些早期汽车在继承蒸汽动力优点的同时，也承袭了它的缺点。

column1: The boilers had to be lit by hand, and they required about twenty minutes to build up pressure before they could be driven.
column2: 锅炉要靠人工点火，还得等大约二十分钟，等压力升起来，车才能开走。

column1: Furthermore, their water reservoirs only lasted for about thirty miles before needing replenishment.
column2: 而且，储水箱里的水只够跑大约三十英里，之后就必须补水。

column1: Despite such shortcomings, these newly designed self-propelled carriages offered quick transportation, and by the early 1900s it was not uncommon to see such machines shuttling wealthy citizens around town.
column2: 尽管有这些缺点，新设计的自驱车仍能提供快捷的交通服务。到20世纪初，经常能看见它们载着富人在城里来来往往。

column1: But the glory days of steam cars were few.
column2: 不过，蒸汽汽车风光的日子并不长。

column1: A new technology called the Internal Combustion Engine soon appeared, which offered the ability to drive down the road just moments after starting up.
column2: 一种名叫内燃机的新技术很快问世，它让车子在发动后片刻就能上路行驶。
column6: drive down the road|沿路行驶

column1: At first, these noisy gasoline cars were unpopular because they were more complicated to operate and they had difficult hand-crank starters, which were known to break arms when the engines backfired.
column2: 起初，这些吵闹的汽油车并不受欢迎，因为它们操作起来更复杂，手摇启动器也难用；发动机回火时，启动摇柄还曾把人的手臂打骨折。

column1: But in 1912 General Motors introduced the electric starter, and over the following few years steam power was gradually phased out.
column2: 但在1912年，通用汽车公司推出了电启动器。在此后的几年里，蒸汽动力逐渐遭到淘汰。

column1: Even as the market was declining, four brothers made one last effort to rekindle the technology.
column2: 就在市场萎缩之际，四兄弟为复兴这项技术作了最后一次努力。

column1: Between 1906 and 1909, while still attending high school, Abner Doble and his three brothers built their first steam car in their parents’ basement.
column2: 1906年至1909年间，艾布纳·多布尔和他的三个兄弟还在读高中，就在父母家的地下室里造出了他们的第一辆蒸汽汽车。

column1: It comprised parts taken from a wrecked early steam car but reconfigured to drive an engine of their own design.
column2: 这辆车由从一辆损毁的早期蒸汽汽车上拆下的零件组成；他们重新配置了这些零件，用来驱动自己设计的发动机。
column8: of their own design|自行设计的

column1: Though it did not run well, the Doble brothers went on to build a second and third prototype in the following years.
column2: 虽然这辆车运行得不太好，但在随后的几年里，多布尔兄弟接着造出了第二辆和第三辆原型车。
column6: in the following years|在随后的几年里

column1: Though the Doble boys’ third prototype, nicknamed the Model B, still lacked the convenience of an internal combustion engine, it drew the attention of automobile trade magazines due to its numerous improvements over previous steam cars.
column2: 多布尔兄弟的第三辆原型车有个别称，叫“B型”。虽然它使用起来仍不如内燃机方便，但与以往的蒸汽汽车相比，它有许多改进，因此引起了汽车行业杂志的注意。
column8: drew the attention of|引起……的注意

column1: The Model B proved to be superior to gasoline automobiles in many ways.
column2: 事实证明，B型车在许多方面都优于汽油车。

column1: Its high-pressure steam drove the engine pistons in virtual silence, in contrast to clattering gas engines which emitted the aroma of burned hydrocarbons.
column2: 它利用高压蒸汽驱动发动机活塞，运转时近乎无声。相比之下，汽油发动机哐当作响，还散发着碳氢化合物燃烧的气味。

column1: Perhaps most impressively, the Model B was amazingly swift.
column2: 也许最令人赞叹的，是B型车快得惊人。

column1: It could accelerate from zero to sixty miles per hour in just fifteen seconds, a feat described as ‘remarkable acceleration’ by Automobile magazine in 1914.
column2: 它只需15秒就能从静止加速到时速60英里，1914年《汽车》杂志称这一表现为“非凡的加速性能”。

column1: The following year Abner Doble drove the Model B from Massachusetts to Detroit in order to seek investment in his automobile design, which he used to open the General Engineering Company.
column2: 第二年，艾布纳·多布尔开着B型车从马萨诸塞州驶往底特律，为自己的汽车设计寻求投资，并用筹得的资金创办了通用工程公司。
column7: General Engineering Company|通用工程公司

column1: He and his brothers immediately began working on the Model C, which was intended to expand upon the innovations of the Model B.
column2: 他和兄弟们马上着手研制C型车，希望在B型车已有的创新基础上更进一步。
column6: expand upon|在……基础上进一步发展

column1: The brothers added features such as a key-based ignition in the cabin, eliminating the need for the operator to manually ignite the boiler.
column2: 兄弟们给车子增加了驾驶室内钥匙点火等功能，驾驶者不再需要手动点燃锅炉。

column1: With these enhancements, the Dobles’ new car company promised a steam vehicle which would provide all of the convenience of a gasoline car, but with much greater speed, much simpler driving controls, and a virtually silent powerplant.
column2: 经过这些改进，多布尔兄弟新成立的汽车公司承诺，其蒸汽车能像汽油车一样使用方便，而且车速快得多，驾驶操控简单得多，动力装置也几乎没有声音。

column1: By the following April, the General Engineering Company had received 5,390 deposits for Doble Detroits, which were scheduled for delivery in early 1918.
column2: 到次年4月，通用工程公司已收到5,390笔订购多布尔底特律车型的订金，按计划这些车将在1918年初交付。
column3: By the following April|到次年四月

column1: Later that year Abner Doble delivered unhappy news to those eagerly awaiting the delivery of their modern new cars.
column2: 那年晚些时候，艾布纳·多布尔给那些急切等待新式汽车交付的买主带来了坏消息。
column3: Later that year|那年晚些时候

column1: Those buyers who received the handful of completed cars complained that the vehicles were sluggish and erratic, sometimes going in reverse when they should go forward.
column2: 造好的车只有寥寥几辆。收到车的买主抱怨说，车子反应迟钝，运行也不稳定，有时明明应当前进，却反倒向后开。

column1: The new engine design, though innovative, was still plagued with serious glitches.
column2: 新发动机的设计固然新颖，却仍受到严重故障的困扰。

column1: The brothers made one final attempt to produce a viable steam automobile.
column2: 兄弟们最后又尝试了一次，想造出一款切实可用的蒸汽汽车。

column1: In early 1924, the Doble brothers shipped a Model E to New York City to be road-tested by the Automobile Club of America.
column2: 1924年初，多布尔兄弟把一辆E型车运往纽约市，交由美国汽车俱乐部进行道路测试。
column5: Automobile Club of America|美国汽车俱乐部

column1: After sitting overnight in freezing temperatures, the car was pushed out into the road and left to sit for over an hour in the frosty morning air.
column2: 这辆车在冰冻气温下停放了一夜，又被推到路上，在结霜的清晨空气中再停放一个多小时。
column7: for over an hour|一个多小时

column1: At the turn of the key, the boiler lit and reached its operating pressure inside of forty seconds.
column2: 钥匙一转，锅炉就点着了，在四十秒之内便达到工作压力。
column3: At the turn of the key|钥匙一转

column1: As they drove the test vehicle further, they found that its evenly distributed weight lent it surprisingly good handling, even though it was so heavy.
column2: 随着测试继续进行，他们发现，尽管车子很重，均匀的重量分布却使它具有出人意料的良好操控性。

column1: As the new Doble steamer was further developed and tested, its maximum speed was pushed to over a hundred miles per hour, and it achieved about fifteen miles per gallon of kerosene with negligible emissions.
column2: 随着多布尔的新蒸汽车得到进一步改进和测试，它的最高时速突破了100英里，每加仑煤油可行驶约15英里，排放量微乎其微。

column1: Sadly, the Dobles’ brilliant steam car never was a financial success.
column2: 遗憾的是，多布尔兄弟这款出色的蒸汽汽车在经济上始终没有获得成功。

column1: Priced at around $18,000 in 1924, it was popular only among the very wealthy.
column2: 1924年它的售价约为18,000美元，只在十分富裕的人中受欢迎。
column6: the very wealthy|十分富裕的人

column1: Plus, it is said that no two Model Es were quite the same, because Abner Doble tinkered endlessly with the design.
column2: 此外，据说没有哪两辆E型车完全一样，因为艾布纳·多布尔总是对设计修修改改。

column1: By the time the company folded in 1931, fewer than fifty of the amazing Model E steam cars had been produced.
column2: 到公司于1931年倒闭时，这款令人惊叹的E型蒸汽汽车总共还没有生产到50辆。

column1: For his whole career, until his death in 1961, Abner Doble remained adamant that steam-powered automobiles were at least equal to gasoline cars, if not superior.
column2: 在自己整个职业生涯中，直至1961年去世，艾布纳·多布尔始终坚信，蒸汽车即便不胜过汽油车，也至少与之不相上下。

column1: Given the evidence, he may have been right.
column2: 从现有证据看，他也许是对的。

column1: Many of the Model E Dobles which have survived are still in good working condition, some having been driven over half a million miles with only normal maintenance.
column2: 现存的多布尔E型车中，许多仍能正常运行，有的只经过常规保养，就已经行驶了50多万英里。
column4: in good working condition|运行状况良好

column1: Astonishingly, an unmodified Doble Model E runs clean enough to pass the emissions laws in California today, and they are pretty strict.
column2: 令人惊讶的是，一辆没有改装过的多布尔E型车，运行时的排放足够低，能满足加利福尼亚州现行的排放法规，而这些规定相当严格。

column1: It is true that the technology poses some difficult problems, but you cannot help but wonder how efficient a steam car might be with the benefit of modern materials and computers.
column2: 这种技术确实面临一些难题，但人们还是忍不住会想，借助现代材料和计算机，蒸汽汽车的效率究竟能高到什么程度？

column1: Under the current pressure to improve automotive performance and reduce emissions, it is not unthinkable that the steam car may rise again.
column2: 眼下，在提高汽车性能、减少排放的压力下，蒸汽汽车再度兴起也并非不可想象。
